This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 to 3 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 09.05.2020 at about 11.00 a.m. he had been riding Honda Shine motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA 02U637 along with his wife by name Swati as pillion rider near Doddahasala Village Gate, KolarBangarpet main road, Kolar Taluk & District, a Honda Accord Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MC4192 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed his motor cycle, due to the said accident, himself and his wife have sustained SCCH5 grievous injuries and his motor cycle is also extensively damaged.
Immediately after the accident he was taken to S.N.R. Hospital Kolar, wherein he took treatment as outpatient.

Further due to accident, he has suffered severe sensory neural hearing loss to both the ears to the extent of 75%, for which has spent an amount of Rs.5,00,000/ towards hospital charges and he requires future medical expenses for hearing impairment, for which he requires Rs.15,00,000/ including other incidental expenses.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 38 years, hale and healthy, he is practicing advocate at Bengaluru, Kolar and Budikote, thereby earning Rs.40,000/ p.m., due to this accident he is not Rajkumar vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171889555/
2 able to attend to his work and lost his income during the period of treatment and future earning capacity, he has became SCCH5 handicapped to a larger extent due to hearing impairment, he has suffered permanent disablement.

sentences.text: Out of this accident crime No.174/2020 is registered against the said car before the Kolar Rural Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
R1 is the insurer, R2 is the owner, R3 is insured of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.30,00,000/.
4.

On service of notice, R1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, he has admitted issuance of policy in respect of Hond Accord Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MC4192, further the driver of the insured vehicle has no valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149 of SCCH5 M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Further submitted that, petitioner who is rider and pillion rider are not wearing helmet on the date of the accident, Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. R2/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioner, the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA01MC4192 is belongs to him and same was insured with R2, the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
R3/insurer has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
SCCH5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 09.05.2020 at about 11.00 a.m. when petitioner and his wife were proceeding from Kolar to Budikote in Honda Shine motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA02U637 at that time, near Doddahasala Village Ghat, Kolar Bangarpet Main Road, due to rash and negligent driving of Honda Accord Car bearing Reg.No.KA01MC4192, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. Whether the owner of the offending vehicle has discharged his initial burden by way of producing relevant documents?
4. What order or award?

sentences.text: In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1: In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief SCCH5 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of statement is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.
10 . The counsel for R1 has not crossexamined the PW1, counsel for R2 has crossexamined the PW1, wherein not disputed the place, date and time of the accident.
Further suggested that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the petitioner, but such suggestion is denied by him.
Further suggested that, in order to claim the compensation, false case is created, such suggestion is also denied.
SCCH5 11.

The police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver by name Elbin Savio, accordinlgy charge sheet is filed against him for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence.
Considering the same, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver,
Hence, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2: As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 38 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of driving license marked as Ex.P.12, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 09.04.1982 and the alleged accident is occurred on 09.05.2020, accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 SCCH5 his age is considered about 39 years as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: As per his case, he is practicing advocate at Bengaluru, Kolar and Budikote, thereby drawing salary of Rs.40,000/ p.m.

, to prove the said fact, he has furnished copy Advocate ID Card marked as Ex.P.9.
14.
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained abrasions over right wrist and over left wrist, abrasion over forehead, right ankle joint and over left ankle.
In this regard he has produced copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5 issued by S.N.R. District Hospital Kolar, wherein it is clearly mentioned that, injuries are simple in nature.
Further he has furnished OPD slip along with Xray Films marked as Ex.P.11, photographs are marked as Ex.P.13.

Petitioner has produced copy of disability certificate marked as Ex.P.10.
SCCH5 15.
Further petitioner has not examined the Doctor regarding the nature of the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
It goes to show that petitioner has sustained only simple injuries.

The wound certificate support the version of the Investigation Officer, but petitioner has furnished copy of the disability certificate issued by the Medical Authority Kolar, accordingly he had 75% permanent disability in relation to his ears, hand, fingers, both ears as per guidelines (S.O 76/E) Guidelines for Assessment of various specified disabilities notified on 04.01.2018
, it goes to show that there is very minute impairment in earing capacity, there is no injury to the ears.
Furthermore Doctor is not examined.
Under such circumstances, said certificate is not helpful to the petitioner.
SCCH5 16.

Further as per case of the petitioner, he is advocate aged about 38 years, practicing at various courts, due to this accident, his income is minimised, but to prove the said facts, there is no evidence on record except his oral say.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.25,000/ on account of loss of disability.
Furthermore there is no medical bill, under such circumstances, he is not entitled for any other reliefs under other heads except the above said global compensation.
17. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.25,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
SCCH5 18.

In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.140521923110041400 which is valid for the period from 19.05.2019 to 18.05.2020, the alleged accident was occurred on 09.05.2020, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further there is no dispute about holding of driving license by the driver of the offending vehicle so that, R1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: R2/owner has appeared, but not given any evidence and not furnished any documents to shift the liability against R1, but it is noticed that, at the time of accident car driver had effective driving licence SCCH5 and which bears the insurance policy issued by the R1 which was in force, said fact is admitted by the R1.

sentences.text: Considering the same, I have answered Issue No.3 in the affirmative.

20. Issue No.4: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.25,000/
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through epayment directly to his SCCH5 account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
